record.original_question: Let 1 < a1 < a2 < ... be an infinite sequence of integers with no three-term arithmetic progression. Must the reciprocal sum sum_{n>1} 1/a_n always be less than 2, and is the map sending such a sequence to its reciprocal sum bijective? More generally, if a sequence is constructed to avoid tuples satisfying a given functional relation f(a_{i1},...,a_{im}) = a_{i,m+1}, determine the maximum possible reciprocal sum.

evidence.quote: Let 1 < a1 < a2 < ... be an infinite sequence of integers such that any three members do not constitute an arithmetical progression. Is it true that always ... < 2? Is the function S({an}n>1) = sum 1/an bijective?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Call a strictly increasing infinite sequence of integers 1 < a_1 < a_2 < a_3 < ... "3-AP-free" if it contains no three-term arithmetic progression, i.e., there are no indices i < j < k with a_i + a_k = 2 a_j. For such a sequence, define its reciprocal sum

  S({a_n}) = sum_{n >= 1} 1/a_n.

(a) Is it true that S({a_n}) < 2 for every 3-AP-free sequence?

(b) Is the map S, sending each 3-AP-free sequence to its reciprocal sum, injective (i.e., do distinct 3-AP-free sequences give distinct reciprocal sums)?

(c) More generally, fix an integer m >= 1 and a function f : Z^m -> Z. Call a strictly increasing infinite integer sequence "f-free" if there are no indices i_1 < i_2 < ... < i_m < i_{m+1} with f(a_{i_1}, ..., a_{i_m}) = a_{i_{m+1}}. Determine

  sup { sum_{n >= 1} 1/a_n : (a_n) is f-free },

i.e., the maximum possible reciprocal sum of an f-free sequence, as a function of f.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of bounding the reciprocal sum of 3-term-arithmetic-progression-free sequences is a classical question of Erdős. While the related Erdős–Turán conjecture for 3-APs (divergent reciprocal sum implies a 3-AP) was established by Bloom–Sisask in 2020, the specific quantitative question of whether the reciprocal sum of every 3-AP-free sequence is strictly less than 2, and whether the map from 3-AP-free sequences to their reciprocal sums is injective, does not appear to have been resolved. The general functional-relation extremal version also appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Erdős conjecture on arithmetic progressions
status_evidence.snippet: Bloom and Sisask proved the conjecture for k=3 (sets with divergent reciprocal sum contain a 3-AP).
status_evidence.claim: Qualitative reciprocal-sum question for 3-APs resolved 2020, but quantitative bound <2 and bijectivity of S not addressed.

status_evidence.title: Reciprocal sums and counting functions - Alex Rice
status_evidence.snippet: Survey on reciprocal sums of progression-free sequences; bounds discussed but exact extremal value not determined.
status_evidence.claim: Sharp bound for reciprocal sum of 3-AP-free sequences remains open.
